subtitle: Garlic, oil, and pasta — emulsified the right way
description: Garlic, oil, and pasta — emulsified the right way. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Boil pasta in well-salted water
steps.instruction: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil with salt that tastes like the sea. Add spaghetti and stir once. Cook 1 minute shy of package directions — the pasta finishes in the skillet.

steps.title: Infuse garlic oil gently
steps.instruction: While pasta cooks, combine ¾ cup olive oil and sliced garlic in a large skillet over medium heat. Add pepper flakes. Cook slowly until garlic is pale gold and fragrant, not brown — brown garlic turns bitter fast. If it darkens, pull the pan off heat for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Toss pasta off heat with starchy water
steps.instruction: Reserve 2 cups pasta water, then drain spaghetti. Transfer pasta to the skillet off heat. Add ½ cup pasta water and remaining ¼ cup olive oil. Toss vigorously 1–2 minutes until the oil emulsifies into a glossy, clingy sauce that coats every strand.

steps.title: Serve immediately
steps.instruction: Fold in parsley and taste for salt. Portion into bowls right away — aglio e olio waits for no one. Pass Parmesan at the line if your crew wants it; the dish is traditionally cheese-optional.

proTips: Assign one cook to proteins and one to sides — rookies stay on timing, not multitasking.
Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Spaghetti Aglio e Olio for the Hall with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Spaghetti Aglio e Olio for the Hall on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Garlic, oil, and pasta — emulsified the right way. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.
substitutions: Any short pasta shape works — penne, rigatoni, or spaghetti.
